title: bug: a trailing-newline database password silently initializes a different PostgreSQL credential
description:
Found during parent task-7693a195c01e45088b8545478aebd51f step6 live probe (full reproducible source in its comments): postgres:17-alpine starts healthy with a trailing-newline POSTGRES_PASSWORD but TCP psql using the exact supplied bytes fails authentication, before and after controlled-3. Normal and space/$/trailing-space controls authenticate, wrong-password controls refuse; all disposable resources removed.
Choose explicit fail-closed validation or supported exact-byte delivery at the owning input/init boundary; do not repair inline in the metadata-secrecy leaf. No value-bearing evidence may be persisted.
definitionOfDone: Reproduce against the actual generated scaffold and pin the precise unsupported-input or authentication boundary without logging planted values.

Reject unsupported newline-bearing database passwords explicitly before successful initialization, or demonstrate exact-byte authentication for them; retain normal/special-character positive controls, wrong-password rejection, and complete teardown.

implementationPlan.description:
CONFIRM THE BOUNDARY BEFORE YOU WRITE ANYTHING, BECAUSE THE OBVIOUS FIX GUARDS NOTHING. NO EDITS.

THIS ROW IS GATED. `dependsOn` names task-7693a195c01e45088b8545478aebd51f ("the compose db service stops carrying POSTGRES_PASSWORD in Config.Env"), which owns EVERY file this row edits and whose work is UNCOMMITTED IN THE TREE. Confirm it reached DONE via get_context.epicSiblings before touching anything; the runtime withholds this row from WORKING claims until then. If you are somehow holding it early, release it rather than editing around a peer's dirt.

CONFIRM WHERE THE PASSWORD COMES FROM, by reading:
- controlled-profile-root-templates.ts:117-123 emits `.env.example` with `POSTGRES_PASSWORD=CHANGE_ME` under `# Copy to .env and replace every CHANGE_ME`.
- The generated compose at :232-265 reads it through compose's own dotenv load: `secrets: POSTGRES_PASSWORD: environment: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:+POSTGRES_PASSWORD}`, target `postgres_password`, with `POSTGRES_PASSWORD_FILE: /run/secrets/postgres_password` on the db service.
The operator authors that `.env` BY HAND. The daemon's environment store is not in this path.

CONFIRM THE STORE IS THE WRONG PLACE, because it is where a reader's instinct goes and it is well built for exactly this shape. `deploy-candidate-environment.ts` delivers the store's variables to the DEPLOYED CANDIDATE at `/run/moe/env`, and `encodeCandidateEnvironment` (:72-76) single-quotes every value with the complete `'\''` encoding, so `set -a; . /run/moe/env` round-trips a newline VERBATIM. A newline-bearing value is delivered CORRECTLY there, and multi-line values are legitimate on that path — environment-contracts.ts:45 says the 4 KiB bound "comfortably holds a private key", and a PEM key is multi-line. So: do not add a code to `ENVIRONMENT_CODE_LAYERS`, and do not write a blanket newline ban on environment values. Record this measurement in your step note; it is the finding this row turns on.

CONFIRM THE LOSS IS INSIDE THE IMAGE. The postgres entrypoint's `file_env` reads the secret with `$(< "$file")`, and command substitution strips ALL trailing newlines. The sibling already measured the mounted file is byte-identical to the supplied value while authentication with those bytes fails, so delivery is exact and the entrypoint is where the byte goes. That closes DoD 2's second branch: exact-byte authentication is not achievable from outside the image, so the answer is fail-closed validation. Say so explicitly rather than leaving the branch open.

COUNT THE VERSION LITERAL SITES: exactly four. live-new-product.tsx:49 and live-new-product.test.tsx:52 (both `"controlled-3"`, hand-transcribed mirrors under apps/control-room), plus the daemon's definition in controlled-profile-generator.ts and its assertion in controlled-profile-generator.test.ts. The ~30 other `CONTROLLED_PROFILE_VERSION` hits are IMPORTS and need no edit — verify that rather than editing them.

REFUSE BEFORE INITIALISATION, AT THE ONLY SEAM THAT SEES THE TRUE BYTES (controlled-profile-root-templates.ts).

Add a guard service to the generated `docker-compose.yml` that reads the mounted secret and refuses when it contains a newline, and make the db service wait for it:
- The guard mounts the SAME secret (`source: POSTGRES_PASSWORD`, `target: postgres_password`). The mounted file carries EXACT bytes — the sibling measured byte equality — so this is the one place the true value is visible before the entrypoint mangles it.
- The check counts newlines and prints none of the value: `wc -l < /run/secrets/postgres_password` is 0 for a value with no newline anywhere. Refuse with a nonzero exit and a message that names POSTGRES_PASSWORD and says a newline is not supported, and says WHY in one clause — the database initialises the value without its trailing newline, so the credential the operator holds is not the credential the database has.
- Reuse `postgres:17-alpine`, already pulled for the db service, so the guard costs no extra image.
- Gate the db on it with `depends_on: { <guard>: { condition: service_completed_successfully } }`.

SCOPE IT TO THIS SECRET, NOT TO ENVIRONMENT VALUES IN GENERAL. Step 1 measured why: the candidate delivery path round-trips newlines correctly and multi-line values are legitimate there. This guard is about one value whose consumer cannot round-trip it.

NEVER PRINT THE VALUE (epic rail 3, and both DoD clauses). `wc -l` reports a count; do not `cat`, do not echo the file, do not interpolate it into the message. Say the same thing in the compose comment so the next editor does not reach for `echo`.

DO NOT RESURRECT THE `x-` FIELD. `${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:?...}` in an `x-` key refuses correctly on unset but LEAKS the supplied value into `docker compose config` — measured on the sibling row (its comment-3e35496a) and rejected there.

DO NOT WEAKEN THE UNSET GUARD. The sibling's measured refusal must survive verbatim: `docker compose up --detach db` with unset AND empty exits 1 with stderr exactly `secret "POSTGRES_PASSWORD" must declare either ` + "`file`" + ` or ` + "`environment`" + `: invalid compose project`. Adding a service the db depends on must not change it; step 4 re-measures it.

BUMP THE PROFILE VERSION IN ALL FOUR PLACES AND LET THE GOLDENS FOLLOW.

The emitted profile changed shape, so `CONTROLLED_PROFILE_VERSION` moves to `controlled-4` in the four literal sites step 1 enumerated: the daemon definition in controlled-profile-generator.ts, its assertion in controlled-profile-generator.test.ts, and the two HAND-TRANSCRIBED mirrors under apps/control-room — live-new-product.tsx:49 and live-new-product.test.tsx:52. Update the version-history comment at live-new-product.tsx:45-46, which already records controlled-1 -> controlled-2 (2026-09-06) and controlled-2 -> controlled-3 (db secret delivery, 2026-09-09); add this one with its own one-clause reason.

RE-CENSUS RATHER THAN TRUSTING THIS LIST. `git grep -n "controlled-3"` across ALL file types before and after — epic rail 2 exists because two of the mirrors are invisible to `pnpm test`, `pnpm typecheck` and the daemon leg, so a forgotten one ships two hard-throwing tests behind three green gates. Zero remaining hits outside version-history prose is the bar.

GOLDEN_MANIFEST and EXPECTED_DOCKER_COMPOSE (both in controlled-profile-generator.test.ts) move as a CONSEQUENCE of the compose change. Update them from the actual emitted bytes; never re-bake a golden to silence a red — if a golden moves in a way you cannot explain from your own diff, stop and say so.

GOLDEN_FILE_COUNT moves ONLY if the emitted file count actually changed. This row adds a service to an existing file and adds no file, so it should not move. If it does, you have added a file you did not intend.

ADD THE UNIT-LEVEL ARM HERE, exact-line rather than fuzzy, in the style the file already uses at its POSTGRES_PASSWORD assertions (:191-194): the compose body contains the guard service, the db's `depends_on` names it with `service_completed_successfully`, and the guard's command contains no `cat` and no echo of the secret path's contents.

PROVE IT AGAINST THE ACTUAL GENERATED SCAFFOLD, LIVE (DoD 1 and DoD 2).

ADAPT THE SIBLING'S PROBE; DO NOT WRITE A SECOND HARNESS. Its full source is in task-7693a195's comment-ed461460 (part 1) and comment-3a32dc34 (part 2): it materialises all generated files into a scratch project under `tmpdir()`, runs `docker compose up`, authenticates from the CONTAINER NETWORK ADDRESS with a wrong-password negative control, sweeps `docker inspect` and `compose config` for the planted value by count, and tears down with label-filtered zero-count assertions. Note its recorded correction: a loopback probe was INVALID because the wrong password also succeeded there; the container network address with the negative control is the valid form. Do not regress to loopback.

FOUR CLASSES, and each one is load-bearing:
(a) TRAILING NEWLINE — `docker compose up` now REFUSES at the guard, before the db initialises. Assert the guard's nonzero exit and that its message names POSTGRES_PASSWORD; assert the db container never reached a running state; assert no volume was created that would carry a half-initialised cluster.
(b) NORMAL random value — still authenticates. This is the positive control that stops (a) from being achieved by refusing everything.
(c) SPACE + `$` + TRAILING SPACE — still authenticates. Special characters are supported and must stay supported; only newlines are refused.
(d) WRONG PASSWORD — still refused by postgres with `password authentication failed` (exit 2), proving the auth probe can fail at all.

AND THE UNSET/EMPTY ARM, which step 2 must not have weakened: `docker compose up --detach db` with unset AND with empty exits 1 with the sibling's exact stderr. Quote it verbatim.

NO VALUE-BEARING EVIDENCE MAY BE PERSISTED (the row says so, and epic rail 3). Compare counts and booleans, never values. Do not log the planted value, a prefix of it, a hash of it, or captured output that contains it. Do not commit a fixture carrying one.

TEARDOWN ON EVERY EXIT PATH INCLUDING THE THROWING ONE (epic rail 4): `down --volumes --remove-orphans` exit 0, then label-filtered `docker ps --all --quiet`, `volume ls --quiet` and `network ls --quiet` all counting ZERO, then the scratch directory removed with its parent asserted to be `tmpdir()`. A probe that leaks a container makes every later gate on this board inadmissible.

THE GATES, BOTH LEGS, THEN THE ADVERSARIAL PASS.

RUN BOTH AND QUOTE BOTH COUNT LINES: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` and `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, each EXIT 0. The control-room leg is MANDATORY, not optional (epic rail 2): two of the four version-literal sites live under apps/control-room, which is in NONE of `pnpm test` (the root vitest include has no `apps/**`), `pnpm typecheck`, or the daemon leg. Read the OUTPUT, not the exit code — a `--filter` leg prints "No projects matched the filters" and exits 0, and "0 passed" is exit 0 too, so the `Test Files N passed` count line is the only discriminator.

Also run `pnpm typecheck`. If a repo-wide leg reds at a path this row does not own, attribute it with the path-attributed baseline (repo-wide failures at the merge-base, then at HEAD, the delta intersected with this row's owned paths) and disclose it verbatim rather than fixing it.

COMPLETION RECORD. State plainly which branch of DoD 2 you took and why the other is closed: exact-byte authentication is not achievable from outside the image, because the entrypoint's `file_env` uses `$(< "$file")` and command substitution strips trailing newlines. Put the four probe classes and their outcomes in a row COMMENT — the completion summary truncates silently at 2000 characters and a severed evidence table reads as a skipped gate.

ADVERSARIAL PASS (load `adversarial-self-review`). Ask, in order: does the guard refuse a LEADING or EMBEDDED newline as well as a trailing one, and is that the behaviour you want — `wc -l` counts them all, so say whether that is deliberate? What happens on a host where the guard image cannot start — does the db start anyway, and is that fail-open? Does `service_completed_successfully` behave the way you assume when the guard exits nonzero, or does compose report something an operator will misread? Can the value reach a log through the guard's own stderr on any path? Does `DATABASE_URL` in `.env.example` carry the same hazard, since an operator pastes the same password into it — and if so, is that a comment on this row rather than a new one, per the delivery-bias rail? And the question the filing poses: after this change, can an operator with a trailing-newline password still reach a running database that holds a credential they cannot reproduce?

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
REJECTED, AND IT IS THE ONE THAT LOOKS RIGHT — refuse newline-bearing values in `environment-store.ts` by adding a code to `ENVIRONMENT_CODE_LAYERS`. That slice is beautifully built for exactly this shape (closed code->layer map, fixed prose details, `VALUE` layer already present), which is why it is a trap. It is NOT IN THIS PATH. The generated product's `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` comes from an operator-authored `.env`, copied by hand from `.env.example` (`cp .env.example .env`, replace `CHANGE_ME`) and loaded by `docker compose`'s own dotenv. The daemon's environment store delivers to the DEPLOYED CANDIDATE at `/run/moe/env`, a different container on a different path. A refusal there would guard nothing and would read, to a later grader, as a fix.

REJECTED for a second and independent reason — a blanket newline ban on environment VALUES would be WRONG even where the store IS in the path. `encodeCandidateEnvironment` (deploy-candidate-environment.ts:72-76) wraps every value in POSIX single quotes with the complete `'\''` encoding, and `set -a; . /run/moe/env` sources it, so a newline-bearing value ROUND-TRIPS CORRECTLY there. Multi-line values are legitimate on that path — environment-contracts.ts:45 says the 4 KiB bound "comfortably holds a private key", and a PEM key is multi-line and ends with a newline. Banning newlines globally would break a working, documented case to fix an unrelated one.

REJECTED — "demonstrate exact-byte authentication", the second half of DoD 2. It is not achievable from outside the image. The postgres entrypoint's `file_env` reads the secret with `$(< "$file")`, and command substitution strips ALL trailing newlines by shell construction. The container therefore initialises the value MINUS its trailing newline while the operator holds the value WITH it — which is precisely "silently initializes a different PostgreSQL credential". The sibling's live probe already measured the file itself round-trips byte-exact (`secretRoundTrip` true) while authentication with the supplied bytes fails, so the loss is inside the entrypoint, not in delivery. That leaves fail-closed validation as the only honest branch.

REJECTED — a compose `x-` field carrying `${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:?...}`. Already measured and rejected on the sibling row (its comment-3e35496a): it refuses correctly on unset but LEAKS the supplied value into `docker compose config` (valueMatches 1). Do not resurrect it.

REJECTED — normalising the value by stripping the newline ourselves. That is what postgres already does silently, and silently is the defect. An operator who typed a newline gets a credential they cannot reproduce; they must be told, not corrected.

ACCEPTED — a guard service in the generated compose that reads `/run/secrets/postgres_password` and refuses BEFORE the db initialises, gated by `depends_on: { condition: service_completed_successfully }`. The secret file carries EXACT bytes (measured by the sibling), so the check is exact; `wc -l < file` counts newlines and prints no value; the same `postgres:17-alpine` image is reused so no extra pull. This is the only seam that sees the true bytes, runs before initialisation, and can say so without printing anything.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
THE DEFECT, MECHANISM NAMED. `postgres:17-alpine` reads `POSTGRES_PASSWORD_FILE` through the entrypoint's `file_env`, which uses `$(< "$file")`; command substitution strips ALL trailing newlines. The container initialises the value minus its trailing newline, the operator holds it with one, and every later authentication with the supplied bytes fails while the container reports healthy. The sibling row's live probe measured both halves: the mounted secret file is byte-identical to the supplied value (`secretRoundTrip` true) AND trailing-newline authentication fails BEFORE and AFTER controlled-3, while normal and space/`$`/trailing-space controls authenticate and wrong-password controls refuse with exit 2. So the loss is inside the image's entrypoint, not in delivery, and it predates this epic.

WHERE THE VALUE ACTUALLY COMES FROM, which decides the whole plan. `controlled-profile-root-templates.ts:117-123` emits `.env.example` with `POSTGRES_PASSWORD=CHANGE_ME` and the header `# Copy to .env and replace every CHANGE_ME`. The generated compose (:232-265) reads it through compose's own dotenv load: `secrets: POSTGRES_PASSWORD: environment: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:+POSTGRES_PASSWORD}`, mounted at `/run/secrets/postgres_password`, with `POSTGRES_PASSWORD_FILE` pointing at it. The operator authors that `.env` BY HAND. The daemon's environment store is nowhere in this path.

WHY THE STORE IS THE WRONG BOUNDARY, measured rather than assumed. `deploy-candidate-environment.ts` delivers the store's variables to the deployed CANDIDATE via a bind mount at `/run/moe/env`, sourced with `set -a; . /run/moe/env; set +a`. `encodeCandidateEnvironment` (:72-76) single-quotes every value with the complete `'\''` encoding, so newlines survive verbatim on that path. Its own comment at :68-70 even says which grammar tightenings belong where: "A NUL byte in a value cannot be delivered to any process by any mechanism ... so it is the store's grammar to tighten, not this encoder's." A NEWLINE is not in that category on the candidate path — it is delivered correctly there.

THE SIBLING OWNS EVERY FILE THIS ROW MUST EDIT, AND ITS WORK IS UNCOMMITTED IN THE TREE RIGHT NOW. task-7693a195 ("the compose db service stops carrying POSTGRES_PASSWORD in Config.Env") is WORKING with worker-409b958a, and `git status --porcelain -- apps/daemon/src/repository/controlled-profile/` shows three MODIFIED files: controlled-profile-root-templates.ts, controlled-profile-generator.ts, controlled-profile-generator.test.ts. Its plan also claims apps/control-room/src/v2/products/live-new-product.tsx and .test.tsx. That is this row's entire file set. `dependsOn` is declared against it, so the runtime withholds this row from WORKING claims until it is DONE.

THE VERSION LITERAL LIVES IN FOUR PLACES AND ONLY FOUR. Most of the ~30 `CONTROLLED_PROFILE_VERSION` hits are IMPORTS and need no edit. The literal itself is at live-new-product.tsx:49 and live-new-product.test.tsx:52 (both `"controlled-3"`, hand-transcribed mirrors under apps/control-room), plus the daemon's own definition in controlled-profile-generator.ts and its assertion in controlled-profile-generator.test.ts. GOLDEN_MANIFEST, EXPECTED_DOCKER_COMPOSE and GOLDEN_FILE_COUNT all live in controlled-profile-generator.test.ts.

THE PROBE ALREADY EXISTS. The sibling's comment-ed461460 and comment-3a32dc34 carry the FULL SOURCE of a repeatable live probe: it materialises all 23 generated files into a scratch project, runs `docker compose up`, authenticates from the container network address with a negative wrong-password control, sweeps `docker inspect` and `compose config` for the planted value, and tears every container, volume and network down with label-filtered zero-count assertions. It measures normal, space/`$`/trailing-space and trailing-newline classes. Adapt it; do not write a second harness.
planningNotes.risks:
1. THE STORE-SIDE FIX IS THE OBVIOUS ONE AND IT IS WRONG. `environment-contracts.ts` has a closed code->layer map, a `VALUE` layer and fixed-prose details — everything a newline refusal would need. Adding one there guards nothing, because the operator hand-authors the `.env` this password comes from. If a reviewer or a later worker proposes it, the answer is the measurement, not an argument.

2. A BLANKET NEWLINE BAN BREAKS A WORKING CASE. The candidate delivery path round-trips newlines correctly through POSIX single quoting, and multi-line PEM values are legitimate there. Any rule this row writes must be scoped to the postgres secret, not to environment values in general.

3. THE SIBLING'S WIP IS LIVE IN THE TREE. Three of the five owned files are MODIFIED and uncommitted by worker-409b958a right now. Do not start until task-7693a195 is DONE — the dependency is declared and the runtime enforces it, but if you somehow hold this row early, releasing it is the correct move, never editing around the dirt.

4. NO VALUE MAY BE PRINTED, ANYWHERE. Epic rail 3 and both DoD clauses. The guard uses `wc -l < /run/secrets/postgres_password`, which reports a COUNT; it must never echo the file, and its refusal message names the variable, never the value. The probe must not persist planted values or credential-bearing output — the sibling's harness already gets this right by comparing counts and booleans.

5. THE GUARD MUST NOT MAKE AN UNSET PASSWORD START SILENTLY. The sibling's DoD 3 protects a measured refusal: `docker compose up --detach db` with unset AND empty exits 1 with exactly `secret "POSTGRES_PASSWORD" must declare either \`file\` or \`environment\`: invalid compose project`. Adding a service that depends on the db must not change that — re-run that arm and quote the stderr.

6. A NEW SERVICE MOVES THE GOLDENS AND MAY MOVE GOLDEN_FILE_COUNT. GOLDEN_MANIFEST and EXPECTED_DOCKER_COMPOSE move as a CONSEQUENCE of the change; they are never re-baked to silence a red. GOLDEN_FILE_COUNT moves only if the file count actually changes, and this row adds no file.

7. THE CONTROL-ROOM LEG IS MANDATORY (epic rail 2). Two of the four version-literal sites live under apps/control-room, which is invisible to `pnpm test`, `pnpm typecheck` AND the daemon leg. A forgotten mirror ships two hard-throwing tests behind three green gates.
